title: openai /v1/chat.completions parity: params, roles, stop/logprobs, streaming & function-calls formatting
author: Aisha Kumar
body:
Background and motivation:
We maintain an OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat.completions shim to ease migrations and integration tests for customers. Over time the shim has diverged in small ways (param names, role handling for streaming, stop/logprobs semantics, and structured/function call formatting) which has caused flaky integrations and downstream SDK incompatibilities. This PR completes parity for the most common surface area: request params (temperature/top_p/n/stream), message roles/content/tags, stop sequences and logprobs passthrough, streaming stability for tool/function-calling edges, and structured output formatting to match OpenAI responses.

Summary of changes (high level):
- Normalize incoming OpenAI-style params to our internal request model and add acceptance tests for legacy variants (e.g. `stop` as string or array).
- Fix role normalization during streaming so partial deltas keep the role metadata and stop when function calls are fully emitted. This resolves several customer-reported truncation issues.
- Preserve `logprobs` / token-level scoring in responses when requested and ensure it is emitted in streaming chunks with correct offsets.
- Formalize function/tool call encoding so `name`/`arguments`/`content` match OpenAI's shape; add structured-output validation and fallbacks to previous behavior for backwards compatibility.
- Add comprehensive integration tests and example snippets to the Python and TypeScript SDK compatibility helpers.

Checklist:
- [x] Update request param mapping and validation
- [x] Streaming role/delta stability fixes
- [x] stop sequence handling (string | [string])
- [x] logprobs passthrough across sync/streaming paths
- [x] Function/tool call structured formatting and tests
- [x] Docs and examples updated
- [x] Integration tests added (CI)

Commits summary:
- normalize-openai-params: map temperature/top_p/n/stream/max_tokens and add validation errors for incompatible combos
- streaming-role-stability: keep role metadata in streaming deltas and ensure final chunk emits end_of_message marker
- stop-logprobs: preserve stop token logic and attach token logprobs into token-level events
- function-formatting: produce OpenAI-compatible function call JSON and add serializer/deserializer in openai_compat module
- tests: add integration tests and fixtures for parity cases

Files changed (high-level):
- src/server/openai_compat/chat_completions_handler.rs: main compatibility layer for request/response mapping and streaming glue
- src/runtime/streaming/streamer.rs: fixes to delta emission order and metadata preservation
- src/runtime/token_scorer/logprobs.rs: plumbing to attach token logprobs in streaming chunks
- src/models/function_call.rs: structured function/tool call encoder/decoder
- sdk/python/redwood/openai_compat.py: helper adapters and examples
- sdk/typescript/src/openai_compat.ts: TS adapters and docs examples
- docs/openai-compat.md: documented compatibility guarantees and examples
- tests/integration/openai_parity.rs: new integration test harness with fixtures

Notable implementation details:
- Parameter mapping: we now accept both `stop` as a single string or an array; we normalize to Vec<String> internally and validate maximum length per request.
- Streaming role fix: previously the first streaming delta dropped the role field which broke some SDKs that reconstruct messages from deltas. We now include a `role` field on the first chunk and preserve it in subsequent deltas; finalization emits a `finish_reason` that matches OpenAI's `stop`/`length` values.
- Logprobs: token scoring is expensive; to avoid regressions we only compute logprobs when requested (narrow acceptance). When requested in streaming mode we emit partial `logprobs` alongside tokens using the same event envelope as the final response, keeping offsets consistent.
- Function calls: the compatibility serializer ensures `name` is a string, `arguments` is a JSON string (as OpenAI does) and `content` falls back to empty when absent. We also include a compatibility flag to emit legacy `tool` events for older SDKs.

Backward compatibility and rollout plan:
- This PR is backwards compatible with current API consumers. Where behavior changed (e.g., more strict validation), we add clear error messages and migration notes in docs.
- Deploy as a staged rollout: enable compatibility on a subset of shards for 48h and monitor error rates and integration tests.

Related issues and references:
- Linear: ENG-2218 (chat.completions parity epic), ENG-2240 (streaming stability for functions)
- Support ticket: SUP-987: reported streaming truncation during function calls

Release notes:
- Added OpenAI /v1/chat.completions compatibility for params, roles in streaming deltas, stop sequence handling, logprobs passthrough, and function/tool call formatting. See docs/openai-compat.md for migration notes.

Request for reviewers:
- Please focus review on stream ordering (streamer.rs) and the function call serializer (models/function_call.rs). I added inline comments for tricky spots.

streaming-role-stability: include role in deltas and emit final finish_reason
stop-logprobs: attach token logprobs and fix offset calculation
tests: integration fixtures and SDK examples
review_comments: Liam Chen: please add an explicit test for stop as a single string vs array - otherwise looks good.
Aisha Kumar: added tests/integration/fixture for single-string stop and updated parser. PTAL.
Marisol Ortega: streaming deltas look safer now; one nit on the logprobs formatter (see inline).
Aisha Kumar: addressed Marisol's nit, added range checks and unit tests for negative offsets.
Ben Park: approved — ran local smoke tests with python SDK examples.
release_notes: OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity: accept OpenAI-style params, stable streaming roles/deltas, stop sequence normalization, logprobs passthrough in streaming and sync modes, and OpenAI-compatible function/tool call formatting. See docs/openai-compat.md for details.
notes_for_ops: Staged rollout: enable on 10% of runtime shards for 48h. Watch integration-openai-parity job and streaming error rate dashboard (observability -> openai-compat). If errors spike, rollback via feature flag and revert to previous mapping.
